question: Will there be many Jews?
summary: Genesis 22:17-18 and 26:4 promise Abraham's and Isaac's descendants will be as numerous as the stars of heaven and the sand on the shore. Deuteronomy 4:23-27 threatens that if they make a graven image, Yahweh will scatter them and leave them "few in number among the heathen." One promise is unconditional multiplication; the other is conditional reduction.

reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read the multiplication as historically realized and the "few in number" threat as a conditional, reversible punishment for idolatry that never cancels the covenant itself.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells juxtaposes the two poles directly: the promise of descendants "as the stars of heaven" stands against the threat that they will be scattered and "left few in number," which he lists as a standing contradiction.

excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Casts the threatened reduction/scattering as a conditional punishment for idolatry (the Assyrian and Babylonian captivities), not a reversal of the multiplication promise — the conditional vs. unconditional point the summary names.
